newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police kill two militants in gunbattle.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police kill two militants in gunbattle.

text.p: Egyptian police shot dead two suspected Moslem militants on Tuesday in a gunbattle which took place on the edge of a sugar cane field in southern Egypt, the Interior Ministry said in a statement.
It said the militants had shot at a police convoy between the southern villages of Safay and Gamaliya, some 240 km (150 miles) south of Cairo.
The police returned fire and the bodies of the two unidentified men were found among the sugar cane. Police also found two automatic rifles and several rounds of ammunition.
On Friday Islamist gunmen shot at another police convoy guarding Safay village, killing at least one person.
In a nearby village, they also gunned down two butchers they thought were police informers.
The ministry said police had arrested six people in connection with three other attacks by militants in the south within the past three days.
Earlier on Tuesday and further south, police found the body of a police officer who went missing in the mountains during a sortie in pursuit of Islamist militants, security sources said.
The officer, Lieutenant Tamer Salah Abdelhamid, 23, had fallen from a ridge and broken his neck, they said.
In a gunbattle during the same sortie on Sunday, at least one suspected militant was killed and three seriously wounded, assistant interior minister Abdelwahhab Abazeid told reporters.
The posse of policemen had to abandon pursuit because nine policemen and four of their civilian helpers had sunstroke.
They called in a helicopter on Monday to search for Lieutenant Abdelhamid but the helicopter could not find him. A foot patrol found his body on Tuesday morning, the sources said.
Police believe they were chasing Islamist militants who killed at least five people in two attacks in the nearby Nile valley on Friday evening.
The sortie was into mountains east of the Nile near the town of Sahel Selim, about 330 km (205 miles) south of Cairo.
Police believe the gunmen belong to the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest militant group fighting to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people have been killed since the conflict broke out in early 1992.
